chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umeyr from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding an owned slave who married without the permission of his master, has he disobeyed Allah?' He said: 'He disobeyed his master.' I said, 'Is it prohibited?' He said: 'I do not claim that it is prohibited, and say to him that he should not do it except with the permission of his master.'
ai.seo_question: Is a slave's marriage without master's permission considered haram or just disobedience?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the legal validity of the marriage contract and the moral obligation of obedience to the master. He clarifies that while the marriage is not intrinsically invalid or prohibited (*haram*), the slave commits a sin of disobedience (*'as*) by acting without permission, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the master's right is one of precedence and consent rather than absolute veto power over the contract's validity.
